shortDescription: West African crude trading was subdued on Monday as traders focused on upcoming loading programmes for January, signs of ample supply in the market for December and rising freight rates for some sizes of crude shipment.

children: West African crude trading was subdued on Monday as traders focused on upcoming loading programmes for January, signs of ample supply in the market for December and rising freight rates for some sizes of crude shipment.
There were no West African cargoes bid, offered or traded in the Platts window, a trader said
January's loading schedule from Angola is expected this week, with Nigerian programmes due after
About 8 December-loading Angolan cargoes are still available, a trader said, and about 20 Nigerian cargoes, suggesting ample supply for this point in the monthly trading cycle
Freight rates  on some West African routes steadied on Monday after falling from record highs
(RL-WAFUSG-D130). Rates for Aframaxes - medium-sized crude oil tankers - rose on Monday, another trader said, which could put differentials under pressure
Angolan grades on a free-on-board basis are still valued at a discount to dated Brent, a separate market source said

title: W. Africa Crude — December cargoes still unsold as January programmes in focus
